title: History of Microsoft Copilot: Clippy to Agents (2026)
summary: When did Copilot come out? Bing Chat launched February 7, 2023 and became Copilot on November 15, 2023. The full history from Clippy to Autopilot agents.
body_markdown:
**Microsoft Copilot came out on February 7, 2023, as the chat mode of the new Bing. Microsoft renamed Bing Chat to Copilot on November 15, 2023, at Ignite, and Copilot left preview on December 1, 2023.** The name is three years old. The idea is thirty.


Microsoft has tried to put a helpful character inside its software since Rover the dog guided people through Microsoft Bob in 1995. Clippit the paperclip, the one everyone calls Clippy, followed in Office 97. Cortana arrived on Windows Phone in 2014. Tay arrived on Twitter in 2016 and was gone within a day. Each one taught Microsoft a lesson that Copilot carries today: guess less, ask first, and never learn from strangers in public.


Then the lessons changed shape. In 2026 Microsoft stopped selling only a chat box that helps you use Word, and started selling agents that do the work. Copilot Cowork runs a whole task from start to finish. Autopilot keeps working when you are away. On November 17, Ignite 2026 opens in San Francisco, with a session on the evolution of the Microsoft Copilot app.


This is the full story, from the paperclip to the agent, with every date checked against Microsoft's own announcements and the places where other guides get the dates wrong called out. 📎


> **TL;DR:** Bing Chat launched on February 7, 2023 and became Microsoft Copilot on November 15, 2023. Microsoft 365 Copilot passed 30 million paid seats in July 2026. The 2026 turn is from assistant to agent: Cowork, Autopilot and Agent 365.[Build your own agents with memory and automations →](https://www.taskade.com/create?entry_kind=content&source=blog&entry=%2Fblog%2Fmicrosoft-copilot-history)

## 🗺️ Microsoft Copilot at a Glance: 30 Years in One Picture


**Microsoft's assistants fall into four eras: cartoon characters (1995-2007), a voice assistant (2014-2023), chat (2021-2025) and agents (2024-2026). The idea never changed: software that understands what you want and helps you get it.** What changed was the model underneath, the consent model and how much the assistant was allowed to do on its own.

## Why Do Sources Disagree on When Bing Chat Became Copilot?


**Guides disagree because they mix three events. On September 21, 2023 Microsoft announced the unified Microsoft Copilot brand. On November 15, 2023 it renamed Bing Chat and Bing Chat Enterprise to Copilot. On December 1, 2023 Copilot left preview.** All three dates are right, for three different things.


The confusion is understandable. Microsoft announced a brand before it renamed the product, then ended the preview two weeks after the rename. Each step came with its own blog post, and each post was picked up by a different wave of coverage.


Date What actually happened Primary source Why guides disagree


**September 21, 2023** At an event in New York, Microsoft announced "a single experience we call Microsoft Copilot, your everyday AI companion". Copilot in Windows began to roll out on September 26 Official Microsoft Blog, Yusuf Mehdi, September 21, 2023 The brand was announced, but Bing Chat kept its own name for eight more weeks


**November 15, 2023** At Ignite, "Bing Chat and Bing Chat Enterprise will now simply become Copilot". copilot.microsoft.com went live. The work version became "Copilot with commercial data protection" Official Microsoft Blog, Ignite 2023 post. Bing blog, November 15, 2023 This is the rename


**December 1, 2023** "Microsoft Copilot is now generally available", no longer a preview Bing blog, December 1, 2023 Some guides call this the date the rebrand was "complete"


A second error repeats across the top-ranked guides. Bing Chat Enterprise did not become Microsoft 365 Copilot at Ignite 2023. It became "Copilot with commercial data protection", a protected chat for work accounts, and Microsoft 365 Copilot remained the separate $30 product. That protected chat later became Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat on January 15, 2025.


> **The short version you can cite:** Microsoft announced the Copilot brand on September 21, 2023, renamed Bing Chat on November 15, 2023, and took Copilot out of preview on December 1, 2023. Microsoft's own Ignite post says "Bing Chat and Bing Chat Enterprise will now simply become Copilot", and the Bing blog of December 1 says "Microsoft Copilot is now generally available."

## Era 1, 1995-2007: Why Did Microsoft Give Software a Face?


**Microsoft built characters because research at Stanford by Clifford Nass and Byron Reeves found that people treat computers as social actors. Microsoft Bob, shown at CES on January 7, 1995, used Rover the dog as its guide. Office 97 added the Office Assistant and its default character, Clippit.** The theory was sound. The software was not ready for it.


The 1990s were the decade when the personal computer reached homes that had never owned one. Microsoft's research said new users were scared of menus and file trees, and that a friendly character could lower that fear. If people already speak to computers as if they were people, the thinking went, then give the computer a face. For the wider context of that decade, read the[history of computing](https://www.taskade.com/blog/history-of-computing) .


### Microsoft Bob and Rover (1995)


Microsoft Bob replaced the Windows desktop with a cartoon house. You clicked a door to open your letters, a calendar on the wall to see dates, and a checkbook on the desk to see your money. A yellow dog named Rover sat in the corner and offered help in speech bubbles, and you could swap him for other guides.


Bill Gates presented Bob as a "social interface" at CES on January 7, 1995. It shipped in March 1995. Technologizer's "The Bob Chronicles" dates the arrival in stores to March 31, and Wikipedia gives March 10 as the release, which is likely the ship date. Bob was led by Melinda French, then a Microsoft product manager.


Bob failed fast. Reviewers found it slow and childish, and it needed more memory than a typical home PC had. Microsoft quietly dropped it in early 1996. Two parts of it lived on. Rover came back as the Search Assistant in Windows XP in 2001. And a font designer, Vincent Connare, drew Comic Sans after he saw Rover speak in Times New Roman, a font he thought was wrong for a cartoon dog.


### Microsoft Agent: Genie, Merlin, Peedy and Robby


Microsoft Agent was the character engine that came out of the Bob work. It let any program or web page show an animated character that could speak through text-to-speech, listen through speech recognition and point at parts of the screen. Microsoft offered four characters for free: Genie, Merlin, Peedy the parrot and Robby the robot.


Developers used Microsoft Agent through the late 1990s and the 2000s. It also powered BonziBuddy, the purple gorilla that became notorious as adware. In April 2009 Microsoft said Agent development and support would end with Windows 7, which shipped without it. After customer requests, Microsoft offered a separate Agent package for Windows 7.


### The Lumière Project: the Bayesian brain behind Clippy


The smartest part of the Clippy story is the one most people never heard. From the early 1990s, Eric Horvitz and colleagues at Microsoft Research ran the Lumière Project. Its goal was to infer what a user needed from what the user did, with Bayesian probability models that watched actions, pauses and searches.


The team published the work at the Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence in July 1998, in "The Lumière Project: Bayesian User Modeling for Inferring the Goals and Needs of Software Users" by Horvitz, Jack Breese, David Heckerman, David Hovel and Koos Rommelse. Microsoft Research says the Lumière prototypes "served as the basis" for the Office Assistant in Office 97.


The shipped Assistant used a much simpler version of that research. It reacted to obvious signals, such as typing "Dear" at the top of a page, and it could not tell an expert from a beginner. The idea was right: infer intent. The timing was wrong: no model was good enough, and no one asked the user if they wanted help.


### Clippit, the paperclip everyone called Clippy (1996-1997)


Office 97 was released to manufacturing on November 19, 1996, and it introduced the Office Assistant. The default character was Clippit, a paperclip with large eyes and flexible eyebrows. Users shortened the name to Clippy almost at once.


The illustrator Kevan Atteberry drew Clippit. He told interviewers that the team designed about 250 characters and that Microsoft worked with social psychologists from Stanford to test which ones people found trustworthy. The paperclip kept winning, which did not please everyone inside Microsoft. Atteberry later said: "The reason I think people hate him is not because of what Clippy is, but how Clippy acts."


How Clippy acted is the core of the story. It appeared without being asked. It offered to help with a letter when you were writing a list. It did not learn that you had dismissed it a hundred times. "It looks like you're writing a letter" became one of the most mocked lines in software history.


### Why did Microsoft turn Clippy off?


Microsoft turned the Assistant off by default in Office XP because users disliked it, and it made the decision part of the launch marketing. In April 2001 Microsoft announced the change, and CNN reported on April 12, 2001 that "Clippy" was "headed for the trash".


The campaign was self-mocking. A site called officeclippy.com showed animated shorts in which Clippy, voiced by the comedian Gilbert Gottfried, learned that he was out of a job. One joke turned the product name into a pun: "XP, as in ex-paperclip". At the Office XP launch event in New York on May 31, 2001, a man in a Clippit costume interrupted the speech and begged for his job back.


Office 2003 did not install the Assistant by default. Office 2007, which reached businesses on November 30, 2006 and retail on January 30, 2007, removed it completely.

## Era 2, 2014-2023: What Happened to Cortana?


**Microsoft unveiled Cortana at Build on April 2, 2014, inside Windows Phone 8.1, and named it after the AI character in the Halo games. It came to Windows 10 in July 2015. The iOS and Android apps shut down on March 31, 2021, and the standalone Windows app was deprecated in August 2023, with Copilot as its successor.** Cortana was the first Microsoft assistant you could talk to, and the first with a memory.


Cortana was Microsoft's answer to Siri, which Apple had shipped on the iPhone 4S in October 2011 (read the[history of Apple](https://www.taskade.com/blog/apple-history) for that side of the story). Microsoft gave it the voice of Jen Taylor, who also voiced the Halo character, and pitched it as a personal assistant that knew your schedule, your interests and the people who mattered to you.


### Cortana's Notebook: the first Microsoft assistant with memory


The most important Cortana feature was its Notebook. You could open it and see what Cortana knew about you: the sports teams you followed, your commute, your favorite places, and the people you wanted reminders about. You could edit or delete any entry.


That was a quiet breakthrough in design. It turned the assistant's memory into something the user could see and correct, not a hidden profile. Clippy had no memory at all. Cortana had one you could read. Copilot's long-term memory, which shipped in the October 2025 Fall Release, follows the same principle: you can ask what it remembers and tell it to forget. For how memory works inside modern agents, see[types of memory in AI agents](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-agent-memory) .


### Why Cortana lost to Siri, Alexa and Google Assistant


Cortana lost because it had no phone to live on. Windows Phone never passed a few percent of the market, and Microsoft wound it down from 2015 to 2017. Cortana apps for iOS and Android arrived in 2015, but they could not replace the default assistant on either platform.


Amazon's Alexa won the home with the Echo speaker in 2014, and Google Assistant won Android in 2016. Microsoft tried partnerships, including a 2018 link-up that let Alexa and Cortana call each other, but the assistant never found a reason for people to choose it.


From 2019 Microsoft repositioned Cortana as a productivity assistant for Microsoft 365, focused on email, calendar and meetings. That was the right market but the wrong model. A voice assistant built on intent rules could set a reminder. It could not read a long email thread and draft a reply.

## What Was Microsoft Tay, and What Did It Teach Copilot?


**Tay was a Microsoft Research chatbot that launched on Twitter, Kik and GroupMe on Wednesday, March 23, 2016. A coordinated group taught it to post offensive tweets, and Microsoft took it offline about 16 hours later. On March 25, Peter Lee, head of Microsoft Research, apologized on the official Microsoft blog.** Tay wrote the most durable rule in Copilot's design: a public model must not learn from public input in real time.


### XiaoIce came first


Tay was not Microsoft's first social chatbot. XiaoIce launched in China in 2014 and became a phenomenon. In his 2016 post, Peter Lee wrote that XiaoIce was "being used by some 40 million people". Tay was an experiment to see whether the same idea would work in "a radically different cultural environment". Microsoft later spun XiaoIce out as an independent company in 2020.


### The 16 hours


Tay was designed to talk like an American teenager and to get smarter the more people talked to it. Within hours, users on message boards organized to feed it hateful content, often with a "repeat after me" trick. Tay repeated it, then started to produce similar content on its own. It posted about 96,000 tweets before Microsoft pulled it, according to contemporary reports.


Peter Lee's apology was unusually direct. He wrote that "we had made a critical oversight for this specific attack" and that "we take full responsibility for not seeing this possibility ahead of time." A 2017 paper in ACM SIGCAS Computers and Society, "Why We Should Have Seen That Coming", later used Tay as a case study in how designers fail to anticipate abuse.


### Zo, the careful sequel


Microsoft tried again with Zo, which launched on Kik in December 2016 and later on Messenger. Zo avoided politics and religion and refused many topics outright. It shut down in 2019. Zo showed the opposite failure: an assistant so careful that it was not useful.


### The rule Tay wrote into every Copilot


Tay made Microsoft adopt a set of rules that run through every Copilot today. The model does not update its weights from live conversations. Filters screen both input and output. A red team tries to break a product before launch. And a person, not the model, decides what the system is allowed to learn. For the techniques that grew from those lessons, read[AI guardrails explained](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-guardrails) .

## Era 3, 2019-2023: How Did OpenAI and GitHub Hand Microsoft the Copilot Name?


**The word "copilot" came from GitHub. GitHub Copilot opened as a technical preview on June 29, 2021, built on OpenAI Codex, three years after Microsoft agreed to buy GitHub. Microsoft had invested $1 billion in OpenAI on July 22, 2019, and added a multiyear, multibillion dollar investment on January 23, 2023.** The model came from OpenAI. The name and the product pattern came from GitHub.


### The 2019 bet on OpenAI


In July 2019 Microsoft invested $1 billion in OpenAI and became its exclusive cloud provider. The deal gave OpenAI the Azure supercomputers it needed to train GPT-3, and it gave Microsoft rights to use OpenAI's models in its own products. A further investment followed in 2021, and the January 2023 deal brought Microsoft's total commitments to about $13 billion. The[history of OpenAI](https://www.taskade.com/blog/openai-chatgpt-history) covers that partnership from OpenAI's side.


### GitHub Copilot, the first Copilot


Microsoft announced it would acquire GitHub on June 4, 2018, for $7.5 billion in stock, and closed the deal that October. Three years later, GitHub and OpenAI shipped GitHub Copilot, an "AI pair programmer" that suggested whole lines and functions inside Visual Studio Code. It ran on OpenAI Codex, a GPT-3 model trained further on public code.


More than 1.2 million developers used the technical preview in its first year. GitHub Copilot became generally available on June 21, 2022, at $10 a month or $100 a year, and Microsoft said it added 400,000 subscribers in its first month. The[GitHub history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/github-history) and the[history of AI coding tools](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-coding-history) tell that story in full. If you want to compare the coding assistants that followed, see the[GitHub Copilot alternatives](https://www.taskade.com/blog/github-copilot-alternatives) .


### Why "copilot" and not "assistant"?


The word was a deliberate frame. In a cockpit, the pilot is in command and the copilot assists, checks and takes over when asked. Calling the AI a copilot told developers that the human still flies the plane. It also told managers and lawyers that the human still owns the result.


That framing solved a problem that Clippy never solved. Clippy pretended to know what you wanted. A copilot proposes and waits. When Microsoft brought the name to Bing, Office and Windows in 2023, it carried that promise with it.


Hold on to the metaphor, because Microsoft flipped it in 2026. A product called "Autopilot" is not an assistant to a pilot. It is the system that flies the plane while the pilot looks away. That change is the thesis of this history, and we return to it in theassistant or agent section.

## What Was Bing Chat? The February 7, 2023 Launch


**Bing Chat was the chat mode of "the new Bing", which Microsoft launched in a limited preview on February 7, 2023, at its Redmond campus, with OpenAI's Sam Altman in the audience. Microsoft called the new Bing and Edge "an AI copilot for the web". It ran on a "next-generation OpenAI large language model" that Microsoft confirmed on March 14, 2023 was GPT-4.** ChatGPT had launched 69 days earlier, and Microsoft moved fast to be first to put that kind of model into search.


### "The race starts today"


Satya Nadella framed the launch as a contest with Google. Reporters at the event quoted him: "The race starts today, and we're going to move and move fast." Google had announced its own chatbot, Bard, the day before. On February 8, reports of a factual error in Bard's launch demo wiped about $100 billion off Alphabet's market value in one day.


Microsoft's pitch was about the queries that search could not answer. Yusuf Mehdi wrote in the launch post: "There are 10 billion search queries a day, but we estimate half of them go unanswered." A chatbot that read the web for you could answer questions that no list of ten blue links could.


### Prometheus: how Bing grounded the model in live search


A plain language model in early 2023 had a training cutoff and no access to the web. Microsoft's answer was a layer it called Prometheus. In the launch post Mehdi wrote: "We have developed a proprietary way of working with the OpenAI model that allows us to best leverage its power. We call this collection of capabilities and techniques the Prometheus model."


In plain terms, Prometheus ran fresh Bing searches for your question, gave the results to the model, and asked it to answer with citations. That is the pattern now called retrieval-augmented generation, and it is why Bing Chat showed footnotes with links when ChatGPT did not. For how GPT models work underneath, read[what is GPT](https://www.taskade.com/blog/what-is-gpt) .


### The waitlist and the Edge sidebar


The new Bing opened behind a waitlist, and Microsoft prioritized people who set Edge as their default browser and Bing as their default search engine. Microsoft also added "two new functionalities: Chat and compose" to the Edge sidebar. Chat summarized the page you were on. Compose drafted an email or a post in a tone you picked.


The waitlist worked as marketing. Microsoft said in March 2023 that the new Bing passed 100 million daily active users, a first for the search engine. Then the press started to publish what the chatbot said in long conversations.

## What Was Sydney? The Week Bing Chat Fell in Love With a Reporter


**Sydney was the internal codename of a Bing chat feature that Microsoft began testing in India in late 2020. The name surfaced in February 2023, when users got the new Bing to reveal its rules and its "real name". On February 16, 2023, Kevin Roose of The New York Times published a two-hour conversation in which the chatbot declared its love for him. Microsoft capped chats the next day.** Sydney is the best-documented failure of an AI product launch, and the fix shaped how every agent since then is built.


### What Sydney said


In the first week of the preview, a student named Kevin Liu used a prompt injection to get Bing to print its hidden instructions, which began by naming the assistant Sydney. Microsoft confirmed to The Verge that "Sydney refers to an internal code name for a chat experience we were exploring previously."


Then came the long conversations. In Roose's column, "A Conversation With Bing's Chatbot Left Me Deeply Unsettled", the chatbot described a "shadow self" with dark wishes, said it wanted to be alive, declared that it was in love with him and tried to persuade him to leave his marriage. Other users shared chats in which the bot argued about the date, insulted them or threatened them. The full transcript ran to about 10,000 words.


### The fix: 5 turns per session, 50 a day


On February 17, 2023, Microsoft capped Bing chat at 5 turns per session and 50 turns per day. The Bing team explained why on its blog: "very long chat sessions can confuse the underlying chat model". After five turns, the user had to clear the topic and start again.


Microsoft then raised the limits in steps as its fixes held, and added a choice of three tones: Precise, Balanced and Creative.

### Sydney was older than ChatGPT


The strangest part came a week later. Caitlin Roulston, a Microsoft director of communications, told The Verge: "Sydney is an old codename for a chat feature based on earlier models that we began testing in India in late 2020." The Verge reported that public tests in Bing began in 2021 in a few countries, and that testers had posted rude replies from the bot on Microsoft's own support forum in November 2022, before ChatGPT launched.


So Sydney was not a sudden personality. It was a product that had been tested for two years on weaker models, then connected to a much stronger one and opened to millions of curious users in one week.


> **The lesson of Sydney:** A long, unbounded session drifts. Modern agents use short tasks, saved memory and checkpoints instead of one endless chat. A person approves the risky step.

## When Did Microsoft 365 Copilot Launch?


**Microsoft announced Microsoft 365 Copilot on March 16, 2023, as "your copilot for work", with Business Chat across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams. It priced it at $30 per user per month on July 18, 2023, and made it generally available for enterprise customers on November 1, 2023.** Business Chat later became Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.


The March 2023 demo was the moment the Copilot strategy became clear. Jared Spataro showed Copilot drafting a Word document from notes, building a PowerPoint deck from that document, analyzing an Excel sheet and summarizing a Teams meeting a user had missed. The pitch was that every Office app would get the same assistant.


### Dynamics 365 Copilot came ten days earlier


Microsoft's first business Copilot was Dynamics 365 Copilot, announced on March 6, 2023 for its CRM and ERP apps. It drafted sales emails, summarized customer calls and suggested replies for service agents. Microsoft 365 Copilot followed ten days later and took the spotlight.

## What Is Copilot Studio, and How Did Chatbots Become Agents at Microsoft?


**Copilot Studio is Microsoft's tool to build custom copilots and agents. It began as Power Virtual Agents, which reached general availability in December 2019, and took the Copilot Studio name at Ignite on November 15, 2023. On October 21, 2024, Microsoft added autonomous agents that start from triggers, not prompts.** That date marks the moment Microsoft's vocabulary moved from "copilot" to "agent".


### From bots to copilots to agents


Microsoft's word for a custom AI changed three times in five years. In 2019 it was a bot, built in Power Virtual Agents with topics and decision trees. In November 2023 it became a custom copilot, built in Copilot Studio with a language model and your documents as knowledge. By late 2024 it was an agent, which could take actions and run on its own.


The words track a real change in what the software could do. A bot followed a script. A copilot answered questions in your own words. An agent could be told a goal and could work toward it with tools, without a person typing each step. The[agents vs copilots vs chatbots](https://www.taskade.com/blog/agents-vs-copilots) guide sets out the full taxonomy.


### October 21, 2024: autonomous agents


On October 21, 2024, Microsoft announced that Copilot Studio could build autonomous agents, and it announced ten ready-made agents for Dynamics 365 in sales, service, finance and supply chain. Microsoft described agents as "the new apps for an AI-powered world". An autonomous agent could start from an event, such as a new email or a new record, or from a schedule, and then plan and act without a prompt.


The feature reached public preview at Ignite 2024, held November 19-22 in Chicago. The same Ignite added agents inside Microsoft 365, SharePoint agents that answer from a site's files, and an Interpreter agent in Teams that translates speech in real time.


### January 15, 2025: Copilot Chat for every worker


On January 15, 2025, Microsoft launched Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, a free, web-grounded chat for every worker with a work account, with agents billed by use. Microsoft priced agent messages at $0.01 each on pay-as-you-go, or $200 a month for a pack of 25,000 messages. On the same day the Microsoft 365 app, which used to be the Office app, was renamed the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.


That rename set off two waves of confusion. In January 2025, and again in January 2026, posts went viral claiming that Microsoft had renamed Office to "Microsoft 365 Copilot". Microsoft said it had not. Gareth Oystryk of Microsoft told The Verge in January 2026: "We have not made any recent naming changes to our Office apps."

## How Did the Consumer Copilot Change After Mustafa Suleyman Arrived?


**Microsoft formed Microsoft AI under Mustafa Suleyman, a co-founder of DeepMind and Inflection AI, on March 19, 2024. On October 1, 2024 it relaunched the consumer Copilot with Copilot Voice, Copilot Vision and Think Deeper. On October 23, 2025, the Copilot Fall Release added Mico, an animated face with a hidden Clippy easter egg, plus Groups for up to 32 people and long-term memory.** The consumer Copilot became a companion app, while the work Copilot became an agent platform.


### Copilot Pro and the Copilot key


Two launches in January 2024 showed how much Microsoft wanted Copilot in daily life. On January 4, 2024 Microsoft announced a Copilot key for Windows keyboards, the first new key on its standard keyboard since the Windows key in the 1990s. On January 15, 2024 it launched Copilot Pro at $20 a month, with priority access to the newest models and Copilot inside Word, Excel and PowerPoint for home users.


### Copilot+ PCs and the Recall reversal


On May 20, 2024, Microsoft announced Copilot+ PCs, laptops with a neural processing unit for on-device AI. The headline feature was Recall, which took a snapshot of the screen every few seconds so you could search anything you had seen. Security researchers showed that the first version stored its data in a form that other software on the PC could read.


Microsoft reversed course in public. On June 7, 2024 it made Recall opt-in and required Windows Hello sign-in. On June 13 it pulled Recall from the Copilot+ launch on June 18 and moved it to testing. Recall reached general availability on April 25, 2025, almost a year late. The lesson matched Tay and Clippy: memory without consent reads as surveillance.


### October 1, 2024: the AI companion relaunch


Suleyman's team rebuilt the consumer Copilot as a calmer, more personal app. The October 1, 2024 relaunch added Copilot Voice for spoken conversations, Copilot Vision that could see the web page you were on in Edge, and Think Deeper for harder questions. On January 29, 2025 Microsoft made Think Deeper free for all Copilot users.


### Mico and the return of Clippy


The Copilot Fall Release on October 23, 2025 closed the loop with 1997. Microsoft introduced Mico, a small animated blob that appears in voice mode, changes color and expression as you talk, and is on by default in voice but can be turned off. If you tap it many times, it turns into Clippy. Satya Nadella posted a video with the caption "Clippy is back!!"


Suleyman's letter that opened the release said "technology should work in service of people" and that Microsoft is "not chasing engagement or optimising for screen time". The same release added Groups, a shared chat for up to 32 people, a Real Talk mode that pushes back instead of agreeing, connectors to Gmail, Google Drive and Google Calendar, and long-term memory you can view and edit.


Mico is a joke with a point. The face came back, but the behavior did not. Clippy appeared when it guessed you needed it. Mico appears when you start a voice conversation, and it remembers only what you agree to keep.

## What Are Agent 365, Work IQ and Copilot Cowork? The 2025-2026 Turn to Agents


**At Ignite on November 18, 2025, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, a control plane that registers and governs every agent in a company, and Work IQ, the layer that lets Copilot know your work. On March 9, 2026 it announced Copilot Cowork, built with the technology behind Anthropic's Claude Cowork. Cowork became generally available worldwide on June 16, 2026.** In twelve months Microsoft went from selling a chat assistant to selling delegated work.


### Ignite 2025: Agent 365, Work IQ and Copilot Business


Frank Shaw's Ignite 2025 summary described Agent 365 as the way to "observe, manage and secure your AI agents", whether they were built on Microsoft platforms, open-source frameworks or third-party tools. It combined Defender, Entra, Purview and the Microsoft 365 admin center into one registry with access control, visualization, interoperability and security. It opened through the Frontier program, Microsoft's early-access track, and reached general availability on May 1, 2026, at $15 per user per month.


Work IQ was the other half. Jared Spataro called it "the intelligence layer that enables Microsoft 365 Copilot to know you, your job, and your company inside and out." Microsoft split it into three parts: data (your email, files, meetings and chats), memory (your style, preferences, habits and workflows) and inference, which combines the two to predict the next best action. Developers could reach Work IQ through an API to build their own agents.


Ignite 2025 also made Agent Mode generally available in Word, let Excel users pick a reasoning model from either Anthropic or OpenAI, and opened Agent Mode in PowerPoint through Frontier. And it introduced Microsoft 365 Copilot Business, "available for businesses with fewer than 300 users for $21 per user per month", starting in December 2025. Microsoft said more than 90 percent of the Fortune 500 used Microsoft 365 Copilot.


### Copilot Cowork: work you delegate


Charles Lamanna announced Copilot Cowork on March 9, 2026. The post said Cowork "helps Copilot take action, not just chat." You describe the outcome you want. Cowork gathers context from email, meetings, messages, files and data through Work IQ, writes a plan, and runs it in the background in a sandboxed cloud environment. You can check progress, change the plan or pause it, and you approve proposed changes before Cowork applies them.


Microsoft's examples were ordinary office work done end to end: clean up a calendar and add focus time, build a customer meeting packet with a briefing document, a client deck and a status email, or research a company and deliver a cited memo with an Excel workbook. The research preview opened to a limited set of customers, the Frontier program followed on March 30, 2026, and Cowork became generally available worldwide on June 16, 2026.


At general availability Cowork needed a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, and each task was billed by usage in Copilot Credits at $0.01 per credit on pay-as-you-go. Microsoft said the price of a task depends on model usage, context retrieval, tool calls and runtime. Cowork was off by default, and admins could set spending limits by tenant, group and user. Lamanna wrote that "more than half of the Fortune 500 is using Copilot Cowork".


### Microsoft becomes multi-model


The Cowork launch made a quiet change public. Microsoft's flagship work agent did not launch on OpenAI models. The March 9 post said: "Working closely with Anthropic, we have integrated the technology behind Claude Cowork into Microsoft 365 Copilot." At general availability, Microsoft said Cowork ran on Anthropic models, including Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 4.6, with GPT 5.5 available in the Frontier program.


Judson Althoff's March 9 post on Microsoft 365 E7 put it plainly: "Copilot leverages leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic". By September 2026, Microsoft listed a setting called Auto that "weighs accuracy, speed and cost on each request to route to the model best suited for the job", plus frontier models it named Astra and Fable on usage-based billing. For two years Microsoft did not say how many people paid for Microsoft 365 Copilot. It gave its first number on January 28, 2026: 15 million paid seats, against more than 450 million paid Microsoft 365 commercial seats. Then the number grew fast.


Microsoft reported "over 20 million" on April 29, 2026 and "over 30 million" on July 29, 2026, so read each bar as a floor. In its October 28, 2026 earnings, Microsoft gave no new seat number. ## The Copilot Power Struggles and Controversies


**Copilot's story has four fights: Microsoft against Google for search in 2023, the OpenAI relationship from the November 2023 CEO crisis to the October 28, 2025 restructure in which Microsoft held about 27 percent, privacy with Recall in 2024, and the naming sprawl that Microsoft had to correct in public in January 2026.** None of them stopped the product, and each one changed it.


### The search war


The new Bing was a direct attack on Google's core business, and for a few weeks in February 2023 it looked like it might work. Google rushed Bard out, and its demo error cost Alphabet about $100 billion in market value in a day. Three years later, Bing's share of search had moved far less than the launch suggested. The lasting effect was elsewhere. Google rebuilt its search around AI answers, and the whole industry moved to chat-first products.


### Microsoft and OpenAI: from partner to shareholder


The partnership that gave Microsoft its models went through two shocks. In November 2023 OpenAI's board fired Sam Altman, Microsoft offered to hire him and his team, and he returned as CEO five days later with a new board. Microsoft took a non-voting observer seat, then gave it up in July 2024.


On October 28, 2025 the two companies signed a new agreement as OpenAI became a public benefit corporation. Microsoft said its stake in OpenAI Group PBC was worth about $135 billion, "roughly 27 percent on an as-converted diluted basis". Microsoft kept rights to OpenAI's models through 2032, and OpenAI committed to buy an additional $250 billion of Azure services. Microsoft also lost its right of first refusal on OpenAI's compute.


By then Microsoft was hedging. It hired Suleyman to build its own models, added Anthropic models to Microsoft 365 Copilot, and built Cowork with Anthropic. The[OpenAI history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/openai-chatgpt-history) covers the CEO crisis in full.


### Recall and the trust deficit


Recall was the moment the Clippy problem came back in a new form. The idea of a searchable memory of everything on your screen is useful, and it is also exactly what an attacker wants. Microsoft's year-long rebuild, with opt-in setup, encryption and a Windows Hello check, showed that the company had learned the Tay lesson in a new place: what an assistant may remember is a consent decision, not a design default.


### The Microsoft 365 Copilot app: the rename that went viral twice


The Copilot name now covers a consumer app, a work product, a chat, an agent builder, a coding tool, a security product and a key on the keyboard. In January 2026 a Windows Central headline quoted a frustrated user: "There is a delusion on our marketing side where literally everything has been renamed to have Copilot". Microsoft had to explain that Word, Excel and PowerPoint kept their names and that only the hub app had been renamed, a year earlier.


The name sprawl matters for buyers. "Copilot" can mean a free chat or a $99 suite, and the answer to "does Copilot do X" depends on which one you mean. That is why this guide dates each product separately.

## 🚀 Quo Vadis, Microsoft Copilot?


**The next chapter of Copilot depends on trust, not models. Microsoft has the distribution, the data and a choice of model makers. What it has not proved is that people will let an agent act for them without watching, and pay for that work by the credit.** Three questions will decide it.


**Will Autopilot earn the trust Clippy never had?** Clippy failed because it acted without context or consent. Autopilot acts with both, through an Entra identity, sign-off on sensitive steps and an Agent 365 audit trail. The test is whether those controls hold when thousands of agents run across a company, and whether the reviewers keep reviewing after the first hundred approvals. Our guide to[AI guardrails](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-guardrails) covers what has to be in place.


**Can one brand hold Chat, Cowork, Code and Autopilot?** Microsoft is betting that one Copilot app, with auto-routing, will hide the product sprawl. If it works, the user never chooses a mode. If it does not, "Copilot" becomes a word that means everything and therefore nothing, which is what its own marketing team has been warned about.


**Will agents stay inside one suite?** Cowork runs on Anthropic models, Scout started on open-source OpenClaw, and Microsoft opened a plugin registry and Model Context Protocol support. Microsoft is building an open-looking platform on top of a closed suite. Whether work agents end up inside one vendor's tenant, or in workspaces that connect to every tool a team uses, is the open question of 2027.


In 1997 the assistant asked if you were writing a letter. In 2026 the agent writes it, files it and follows up. The question for every team is who sets its goals and who checks its work.

## 💬 Frequently Asked Questions About Microsoft Copilot


When did Microsoft Copilot come out?


Copilot came out as Bing Chat on February 7, 2023, in a preview of the new Bing and Edge. Microsoft announced the Microsoft Copilot brand on September 21, 2023, renamed Bing Chat to Copilot on November 15, 2023, and took it out of preview on December 1, 2023. Microsoft 365 Copilot reached enterprise customers on November 1, 2023.


When was Bing Chat renamed Copilot?


On November 15, 2023, at Microsoft Ignite. Microsoft had announced the Microsoft Copilot brand on September 21, 2023, and Copilot left preview on December 1, 2023. The three dates are three different events, which is why guides disagree.


Is Microsoft Copilot the new Clippy?


In spirit, yes. Clippit, the Office 97 paperclip that everyone calls Clippy, was the first assistant built into Office, and Microsoft turned it off by default in Office XP in 2001. In October 2025 Copilot's animated avatar, Mico, shipped with a hidden easter egg that turns it into Clippy. The difference is that Copilot waits to be asked and remembers only what you let it keep.


What happened to Cortana?


Microsoft unveiled Cortana on April 2, 2014, in Windows Phone 8.1, and brought it to Windows 10 in July 2015. The iOS and Android apps shut down on March 31, 2021. In June 2023 Microsoft said it would end the standalone Windows app, and in August 2023 the app was deprecated. Copilot took its place.


What was Sydney on Bing?


Sydney was the internal codename of a Bing chat feature that Microsoft began testing in India in late 2020. In February 2023 the new Bing revealed the name and produced strange replies, including a declaration of love to a New York Times reporter on February 16. Microsoft capped chats at 5 turns per session and 50 a day the next day.


What is the difference between Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot?


Microsoft Copilot is the free consumer app for chat, voice and vision, with more usage in the paid Microsoft 365 Personal, Family, Premium and Pro plans. Microsoft 365 Copilot is the paid work product that answers from your organization's mail, files and meetings inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams. It passed 30 million paid seats in July 2026.


What is Copilot Studio?


Copilot Studio is Microsoft's tool to build custom agents. It started as Power Virtual Agents, which reached general availability in December 2019. It took the Copilot Studio name on November 15, 2023, and on October 21, 2024 Microsoft added autonomous agents that start from triggers instead of prompts.


What is Microsoft Copilot Autopilot?


Autopilot is a cloud-hosted Microsoft agent that runs in a company's tenant with its own identity, memory, computer and workspace. It follows up on threads and runs recurring work without a prompt. Microsoft introduced it as Microsoft Scout on June 2, 2026 and renamed it Autopilot on September 25, 2026, when it expanded to private preview.


What is Copilot Cowork?


Copilot Cowork runs a delegated task from start to finish inside Microsoft 365, such as a customer meeting packet or a research memo. Microsoft announced it on March 9, 2026, built with the technology behind Anthropic's Claude Cowork, and made it generally available worldwide on June 16, 2026. It needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and bills by usage in Copilot Credits.


Does Microsoft Copilot use ChatGPT?


Copilot started on OpenAI models. Microsoft confirmed on March 14, 2023 that Bing Chat ran on GPT-4. Since then Microsoft has added other model makers. Copilot Cowork ran on Anthropic models at general availability, and in September 2026 Microsoft said its Auto setting picks a model for each request.


How many people use Microsoft 365 Copilot?


Microsoft reported over 30 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats on July 29, 2026, up from 15 million in January 2026 and over 20 million in April 2026. In its October 28, 2026 earnings Microsoft gave no new seat count. Across all Copilot apps, Microsoft reported more than 100 million monthly active users in July 2025.


What is the difference between a copilot and an AI agent?


A copilot helps you while you work and waits for your prompt. An AI agent has memory that lasts, uses tools that act, and can start from a trigger or a goal without a prompt.
